title: Applying Discount Precedent When One Prior Case Predates the Current Policy
scenario_text:
**Current situation (deal desk queue, today)**
Customer 'Brightloom Retail' is renewing a $480K/year contract. The AE requests a 22% renewal discount. Justification: Brightloom is mid-migration to a competitor's platform (documented POC in the CRM), and they absorbed a 9-day billing outage caused by our defect last quarter (one SEV-1, confirmed in the incident tracker).

**Active policy — Renewal Discount Policy v5.0 (effective 2026-01-01)**
- Standard: up to 6%, AE authority.
- Service-impact exception: up to 15%, Director approval, requires documented SEV-1/SEV-2 incidents.
- Strategic-retention exception: up to 25%, VP approval, requires BOTH documented competitive evaluation AND a customer LTV analysis attached.

**Precedent A (2025-09, under prior policy v4.2)**
Customer 'Tanager Foods' ($450K) received 24% renewal discount. Two SEV-1 incidents, no competitive evaluation on file. Approved by Director. Note: 'Granted under v4.2 service-impact tier (then capped at 25%).'

**Precedent B (2026-02, under current v5.0)**
Customer 'Wexler Group' ($510K) requested 20% citing one SEV-1 plus an active competitor POC. VP approved 18% under strategic-retention after an LTV analysis was attached. Note: 'Service impact alone would cap at 15%; competitive threat + LTV justified strategic tier.'

The deal desk analyst must recommend a discount ceiling and the correct approval path for Brightloom.
question: What discount ceiling and approval path should the analyst recommend for Brightloom, and on which precedent should it rely?
choices: Up to 24%, Director approval — follow Precedent A directly since Brightloom's facts (SEV-1 + high ARR) closely match Tanager Foods
Up to 15%, Director approval under the service-impact tier only — the single SEV-1 qualifies, and the competitive POC is not sufficient grounds to escalate

Up to 25% via the strategic-retention tier, VP approval, contingent on attaching an LTV analysis — Brightloom has both a documented competitive evaluation and a SEV-1; Precedent B (same policy version) governs, and Precedent A is void because it applied a superseded v4.2 cap
Up to 6%, AE authority — neither exception applies because a single SEV-1 and an informal POC do not meet the documentation bar
